text:
sania: Heads-upproposed pattern for onboarding: "lazy normalization" facade that records normalization patches instead of fully materializing normalized binaries by default. Idea is to apply cheap checks + token diff, emit a small patch (mapping + header) and only materialize normalized artifact on-demand (e.g., first serve or when AUTO-FIX is applied). Thoughts?

liam: Interesting. So ingest stays fast for most uploads, storage stays small, but runtime may need to rehydrate. How do we guarantee runtime latency when rehydration needed?

zara: We can pre-warm rehydration during canary or when model is promoted. Also keep an LRU cache of rehydrated artifacts on serving nodes. For enterprise customers that require no rehydration, we can offer a policy to always materialize on ingest.

adele: How does this affect our compatibility checks? If we only emit a patch, we still need to run smoke correctness to catch semantic drift. Do that with CPU probe first?

mike: CPU probe first seems right. Also consider a small quantized reference compiled to CPU (tiny-runtime) that approximates behavior for top-k checks. If that flags, schedule a short GPU micro-run.

ops-bot: Note: current max ingest parallelism is 12. If many rehydrates hit at once, we could see a spike. Recommend a burst queue with backoff and prioritized orgs.

liam: For tokenizer mismatches: propose a two-output remapper: (1) inline remap patch (deterministic mapping used by runtime) and (2) reversible mapping file so we can run replay comparisons on original. If remap changes generation order, mark as "semantic-risk" and force manual review.

sania: Good call. Also add an automated trace replay: pick N representative prompts from sandbox (or user-provided canonical prompts) and compute overlap metrics across original vs patched artifact.

zara: Which metrics are minimal for rollout gating? I'm thinking top-1/top-5 overlap, logprob-delta for gold tokens, and latency delta p50/p95. Keep thresholds configurable per org.

adele: Agree. Also need an explicit policy for header evolution: manifest_version and an allowed-migration table. Runtime must support at least two manifest versions concurrently for a while.

liam: Manifest sketch (compact):
```
manifest_v: 2
model: orgX/coolnet
files: [weights.pt, tokenizer.json]
sha256s: [w:abcd, t:ef01]
tokenizer_sig: tokv2-0b1
patches: [tok-remap-v1]
sanity: {cpu_probe_pass: true, top5_overlap: 0.94}
```

mike: Ops question: are probe results visible to customers? If not, we need clear internal UIs for triage with links to example replays and remap diffs.

sania: Internal-only initially. Triage UI will show remap diff, representative traces, and an action set: APPROVE, REJECT, MARK-AUTO-FIX. Also keep audit log for enterprise compliance.

registry-bot: FYI: adding "patches" indexable field will require registry schema migration. Rolling migration recommended: write-new, read-old+new until clients update.

zara: For policy engine, propose rule-file semantics: ordered list of predicates -> action. Example: if tokenizer_sig mismatch && top1_overlap<0.85 => FAIL. If mismatch && overlap>0.9 => WARN+AUTO-FIX. Keep rules YAML-driven and environment-scoped (prod/test/org).

adele: We should also think about model-abi contract beyond tokenizers: KV cache shape, past-key-value dtype, and preferred compute path tags (e.g., use_fused_attention:true). The patch can include preferred runtime flags and a compatibility level.

liam: Runtime fallback strategy: prefer exact-match adapter, else fall back to shim that applies patch at load-time. Load-time patching must be async-safe and idempotent. Also record which path served a request for observability.

mike: Canary plan: start with internal orgs only. Shadow-run traffic through both patched and raw runtime for 24-72h. Compare overlap and error rate. If within thresholds, flip default for that org. Roll forward global slowly.

sania: Timeline: prototype remapper + lite-CPU probe in 1 week. Rule engine YAML and manifest v2 sketch in parallel. zara will write canary runbook + observability dashboard. Adele will own triage UI wireframe.

ops-bot: Reminder: add capacity margin for rehydration and the small GPU micro-runs. Recommend +15% for the initial canary batch.

zara: One last thought: keep the normalized 'header-first' so runtime can make safe routing decisions (reject, patch-on-load, or use fallback) without reading full weights. That reduces decision latency.

sania: Love it. OK: next check-in in 48h. I'll drop a short RFC draft with diagrams into #eng-ml-docs and link the prototype branch.
